competitive_landscape: Today: Washington State Ferries (diesel, capacity-constrained) plus King County Water Taxi and Kenmore Air seaplanes. The pain is slow crossings, terminal congestion and an ageing diesel fleet — the status quo a faster, cleaner foiling tier improves on.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Cross-Sound and intra-lake commutes (≤16 nm) over flat sheltered water sit inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope — ideal foiling conditions aligned with the state zero-emission mandate.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Carries the San Juan Islands line-haul (~75 nm) and longer island corridors with no charging at small island docks.

precedents.what: A foiling-electric vessel network at national scale (~100 vessels / $100M, 3-year phasing)
precedents.why_it_matters: Proves foiling-electric works as an at-scale transfer-and-island-hopping network, not just a pilot.

regulatory_note: Washington has legislated a hybrid-electric / zero-emission ferry transition with capital funding for electric vessels and shore-charging — clean propulsion is becoming a procurement requirement.
seasonality: Year-round operation in sheltered Sound and lake waters; winter weather and open-strait crossings handled by routing and the hybrid on longer island legs.
summary: Puget Sound is a sheltered inland sea carrying the largest ferry ridership in the United States, with a legislated transition to a zero-emission fleet. Protected water, hard electrification mandate and dense commuter-plus-tourism demand make it one of North America's strongest foiling markets.
tagline: The busiest US ferry system, ready to fly.

use_cases.body: Replace slow diesel ferry legs (Bainbridge ~5 nm, Bremerton ~14 nm, Kingston ~16 nm) with silent, faster, zero-emission foiling commutes.
